before: The writer matched the pieces of a split as moved text only when one inserted run equalled one deleted run, or when inserted runs, one after another, spelled a deleted run exactly. A split that trims its delimiters deletes the text around the pieces, so its pieces were written as new text without the marks that name the characters they copy, and text a peer typed in a piece showed nowhere when the split was undone.
after: Inserted runs in paragraphs the edit creates that, one after another, are stretches of a deleted run in the same order, with less text around them than they cover, are that run moved, and each piece carries the marks of the characters it copies. Text a peer types in a piece of a trimmed split follows it back when the split is undone and forward again on redo.
reason: The writer writes ordinary move marks in the existing docx-text-marks-v1 map, which released replicas of this format already read. No stored field, identity, conflict rule, or canonical mapping changes, so a mixed room converges. A released replica writes a trimmed split without the marks until it upgrades.
